features.name: POS suppliers, purchase bills, supplier ledger, batch / expiry (FEFO), stock valuation, input tax as recorded
features.purpose: Shops record what they buy and what they owe, pharmacies sell by batch with expiry control, and accountants see recorded input tax.
features.expected_behavior: A purchase bill records the supplier's invoice (cost before GST; GST only from a GSTIN supplier; inter / intra by supplier State), adds stock per batch, and adds what is owed; the same supplier bill number cannot be recorded twice; a printed total that differs by more than Re 1 is refused; bills are cancelled (row kept, stock + ledger reversed), never deleted. Batch items sell first-expiry-first-out from non-expired batches; expired stock is never sold; returns go back to the batches sold from. Valuation = average purchase cost before GST (items without a cost are counted as unknown). Input tax is shown 'as recorded' -- eligibility is the accountant's decision.

features.name: POS selling units (box <-> pieces), serial / IMEI tracking, purchase orders, Classic Bluetooth + USB printers, Telugu text in invoice PDFs
features.purpose: Shops sell by box or piece from one stock, phone / appliance shops track each serial or IMEI, owners order from suppliers and receive in parts, and receipts print on the common Classic Bluetooth and USB printers.
features.expected_behavior: A pack has a factor in base units and its own price (or base price x factor) and barcode; stock moves are always in base units and a pack quantity that is not a whole base quantity is refused. Serial items get serials on the purchase bill (IMEI Luhn-checked, duplicates refused), are sold one serial per piece from in-stock serials only, and a credit note must name the sold serial. A purchase order goes draft -> sent -> partially received / received (each receipt records a normal purchase bill) or cancelled. Printers: saved ids classic:<MAC> / usb:<device> go to the native hardware channel, others to BLE; native errors are named, never reported as printed. Non-ASCII text in the invoice PDF is drawn by the phone's text engine as an image.

features.purpose: Everyday measuring helpers on the phone and a shareable visual vehicle report from four photos.
features.expected_behavior: Protractor = angle at a tapped vertex between two tapped arm points on a photo, with an error band from tap accuracy. Magnifier = photo zoom up to 10x (no live preview). Light meter = phone light sensor lux with an approximate band. Sound = microphone dBFS; an approximate dB only after the user calibrates against a real meter; nothing recorded or sent. Vehicle report = front / rear / left / right photos -> one Expert /api/vision/inspect call (domain vehicle) -> on-screen evidence report + PDF with the photos and a 'not a roadworthiness certificate' disclaimer. Every tool is labelled hardware-unverified until a phone test.

features.name: POS shop advance (store credit) that only the customer can spend
features.purpose: A small shop records money a customer paid in advance and uses it for later bills, with the customer approving every change in their own ASKODOX app.
features.expected_behavior: ASKODOX keeps only the record; the money is with the shop, and the terms (en/te, TERMS_VERSION) say ASKODOX is not responsible for it. The owner turns it on after accepting the terms and sets a per-customer limit (default Rs 2,000, never above Rs 10,000). A deposit, a deduction (paying dues from the advance) or a refund is a pending request that counts only after the signed-in number matching the customer's phone approves it (first approval also accepts the terms); the shop can withdraw a pending request but can never approve or lower the balance itself. Requests expire (deposit 7 days, deduction 15 minutes, refund 1 day). The balance never goes below zero or above the limit; a deduction never exceeds what the customer owes. Approved deposits / refunds appear in the day close by method; a deduction is a 'customer_approved' collection with method 'advance'. Entries are append-only.
